result:
If I could change the world in one way—truly, irrevocably—I would dissolve the illusion of separation between people. Not just borders or ideologies, but the deep-seated belief that "I" am fundamentally different from "you." That your pain isn't mine, your joy irrelevant to me, your humanity conditional on your beliefs, skin, or zip code.  

This illusion fuels every war, every hoarded resource, every child hungry while grain rots in silos. It lets us scroll past suffering like background noise. But what if we *felt* each other? Not sentimentally, but viscerally—like how your left hand flinches when your right hand touches fire. If harming another *literally* felt like self-harm, and lifting someone up *physically* lightened your own bones... systems built on exploitation would collapse overnight. Not by force, but because they’d become *unthinkable*.  

The irony? Science already whispers this truth: we share 99.9% identical DNA; our ecosystems entangle us; a virus in one village breathes in every lung. But knowledge isn’t enough. I’d rewrite our nervous systems to *know it in our marrow*.  

The world wouldn’t be "perfect"—conflict might still spark—but it would lack the fuel of indifference. And from that ash, we’d build something closer to home.  

*(No grand utopia promised. Just the end of loneliness as a species.)*
